h: From the shops to the Pier Head
p: Getting here is dead easy. Liverpool Central station is just up the road, James Street station is close by, and Liverpool ONE has its own bus station on the edge of the district. Lime Street, the city's main railway station, is about a fifteen-minute walk, so you really don't need the car.

It's worth allowing more time than you think. Between browsing, eating and stopping for coffee, a few hours disappear quickly, and if you add a film or a round of mini golf, it can easily become a whole afternoon. Weekends and the run-up to Christmas get very busy, so a weekday visit is calmer if you can manage it.

The waterfront is where you'll want to head next. Walk down past Chavasse Park and you'll reach the Royal Albert Dock, home to the Merseyside Maritime Museum, the International Slavery Museum and The Beatles Story. Carry on along the river and you'll find the Pier Head, with the Museum of Liverpool and the famous Royal Liver Building, one of the city's best-loved landmarks.
For a different view of the city, the Mersey Ferries sail from the Pier Head, giving you a brilliant look back at the skyline from the water.

Hungry after all that walking? You've got loads of choice at Liverpool ONE itself, but Bold Street, a short walk up the hill, is famous for its independent cafés and restaurants serving food from around the world.
